verdict.rationale: pnpm documents operations that act on many workspace items at once: filtered task runs across projects, recursive versioning with `pnpm version -r`, and one-line catalog upgrades that apply everywhere. A hands-on user also reports that recursive/parallel commands replaced Lerna. However, there is no first-party reference for recursive run/exec/update semantics, parallelism controls, or bulk operations outside monorepo workspaces. missing for 10: first-party docs for recursive (-r) run/exec/update and filter syntax, documented parallelism and failure handling, bulk operations outside workspaces.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can perform bulk operations across many items at once

citations.quote: filtering to run tasks on just the projects you touched, and a single lockfile for everything
pnpm versions and releases workspace packages with `pnpm change` and `pnpm version -r`.
Define a dependency version once in pnpm-workspace.yaml and reference it as "catalog:" everywhere. One line to upgrade
Recursive/parallel commands replaced my need for Lerna.
